For a bipartite graph (which is 2-colorable, so satisfies ≤ 4 colors), girth ≥ 6 means no 4-cycles (C4) either, since bipartite graphs have no odd cycles, and girth ≥ 6 means shortest cycle ≥ 6.

A bipartite graph with no C4 (girth ≥ 6) on n vertices can have at most roughly O(n^{3/2}) edges. For n=23, this allows quite a few edges.
